audit:secrets_controlplane.summary:
On the secret and IAM side, the unchanged template already covers r5 serving and saving prepared avatars to S3. It does not yet match this box on control-plane registration, and one S3 object is missing.

**What the secret holds.** I did not read the secret directly. The latest evidence is this instance's 2026-09-15 template boot log and /workspace/.musetalk-runtime.env, which the bootstrap script wrote on 2026-09-28. Both show the same 10 keys:
- the musetalk-s3-runtime access key pair
- the bucket lingua-musetalk-s3-storage and the avatars prefix
- region keys
- TRT_ARTIFACT_S3_BUCKET and TRT_ARTIFACT_S3_REGION, which the bootstrap derives from the avatar bucket and region

So HEAD needs no new secret key for r5.

**Live checks, read-only, as musetalk-s3-runtime:**
- The bucket check the boot runs (head_bucket) returns 200.
- The RTX 4070 SUPER bundle and the legacy RTX 3090 bundle are both readable, with size and SHA-256 matching the pinned values.
- avatars/v15 can be listed and read.
- Objects use S3-managed encryption, so the worker needs no KMS rights.

**Blocker: the AMPERE_PLUS (portable) bundle is not in S3 yet (HEAD returns 404).** A 3090 matches only that bundle, so after the push every 3090 boot stops in restore_r5_bundle and the server never starts. Upload it to the exact key in configs/trt_bundles/ampere-plus-r5-srcg50-int8.json before pushing. origin/main is not affected today. If the push has to go first, putting MUSETALK_R5_BUNDLE_RESTORE=auto in the secret lets 3090s boot without the bundle, on the slow eager UNet.

**Gap: the secret has no LINGUA_* keys.** This box registers with the Lingua control plane only because of its local /workspace/.lingua-control-plane.env, which a fresh Vast clone does not have. A Vast worker would boot healthy but never register. Fix it in the secret, not the template:
- Add LINGUA_WORKER_TOKEN, LINGUA_CONTROL_PLANE_BASE_URL and LINGUA_WORKER_DEFAULT_CAPACITY.
- Do not copy this box's per-instance keys (LINGUA_WORKER_BASE_URL, WORKER_ID, VAST_INSTANCE_ID, LINGUA_WORKER_GPU_TYPE), or every worker would register with this box's identity and URL.
- Without a capacity key, workers advertise 1. The 10-call figure was validated only on a 4070 SUPER with its own bundle, not on a 3090 with the portable one.

**Not verified:** whether musetalk-s3-runtime can write to avatars/*, which POST /avatars/prepare needs. A read-only audit cannot test writes, and the IAM policy simulator is denied to this user.

**Needs nothing from the secret:** TURN, which the boot generates from the Vast port mappings.

**Bootstrap (secret-reader) user:** it needs only secretsmanager:GetSecretValue. Its key pair was pasted in plaintext in the request. Rotating it is the one change here that would touch the template.

All S3 calls were read-only: HEAD requests, one list, two 16-byte ranged GETs, one caller-identity lookup and one IAM simulate call, which was denied. No secret values were printed.

checks.item: LINGUA_WORKER_DEFAULT_CAPACITY (calls advertised per worker)
checks.detail: Code: the value is read as max(1, int(env)), default 1. It is sent as both capacity and max_concurrency in every register and heartbeat payload, and used for free_capacity = capacity - max(active_requests, active_sessions_local) in the metrics. The worker itself never rejects a call because of it. Its only local limits are draining/registration, compute slots for SSE/session streams, and WEBRTC_GROUP_MAX_COUNT=12 for groups. How the backend uses the value is unknown (not in this repo); the autoscaling plan intends routing and scale-up on max_concurrency/free_capacity. The docs' example value is "1". Validated so far: 10 concurrent live WebRTC calls pass with margin (5-minute runs, no hour-long soak) and 15 is at the knee (the hour soak failed the strict bar). That was on the RTX 4070 SUPER with its own bundle, in isolation (no Lingua control plane, TURN, STUN or S3), and the limit was the Python event loop, not the GPU. Nothing has been measured for an RTX 3090 on the AMPERE_PLUS bundle, which runs 307 fps vs 401 fps on the build GPU. The code has no per-GPU capacity, so one secret value applies to the whole fleet. Locally the key is present in /workspace/.lingua-control-plane.env (value not printed). It is absent from the secret per the latest evidence, so registered Vast workers would advertise 1.
checks.fix: Add LINGUA_WORKER_DEFAULT_CAPACITY to the secret (no template change), sized for the weakest GPU in the fleet. 10 is validated only for a 4070 SUPER on its own bundle; for the 3090 fleet, run a live test on a 3090 first or start lower.

checks.item: Runtime IAM: avatar write for POST /avatars/prepare
checks.detail: Prepare uploads avatars/v15/<id>.tar.gz with upload_file. At 160-350 MB this is a multipart upload, which needs s3:PutObject, plus s3:AbortMultipartUpload to clean up a failed upload. If the upload is denied, it is logged, AccessDenied is not retried, and prepare still returns 200 with s3_uploaded=false. The avatar then exists only on that worker's disk (./results/v15/avatars inside the repo), which the template deletes at the next boot, and other workers cannot restore it. Write permission for musetalk-s3-runtime is unverified: a read-only audit cannot PutObject, iam:SimulatePrincipalPolicy is denied to that user, and this box's server logs have no upload line. Which identity uploaded the 99 objects in avatars/v15 is unknown; they include this box's 33, uploaded on 2026-09-30, and this box's .runtime/musetalk_overrides.env also sets AWS_PROFILE. The documented runtime policy grants the write.
checks.fix: Check in IAM that musetalk-s3-runtime has s3:PutObject and s3:AbortMultipartUpload on arn:aws:s3:::lingua-musetalk-s3-storage/avatars/*. Alternatively, on the first Vast boot run one POST /avatars/prepare and confirm "s3_uploaded": true (or GET /stats avatar_s3.upload_successes). Fixable in IAM; no template change.

checks.item: S3 verify can fall back to the bootstrap key (the docs say it cannot)
checks.detail: _verify_s3_buckets takes its credentials from os.environ merged with the secret's exports. Under this template os.environ holds the secret-reader pair, so a secret without runtime keys makes head_bucket run as the secret reader. With no S3 rights that returns 403 and the strict boot still fails, just with a different error than the documented one. If the reader ever had S3 rights, the worker would silently use it for all S3 access. The unit test covers only an environment without AWS keys.
checks.fix: Not needed for the template. Optional repo fix: verify using only the secret's exports, not os.environ.

audit:template_trace.summary:
Short answer: the script text is ready. No part of the Vast template needs editing. Two things still stand between the unchanged template and r5 on your RTX 3090s: uploading the portable engine bundle to S3, and pushing main. Push in that order. The bundle has to be uploaded before main is pushed.

At HEAD (e0d0985, after the push), per GPU:
- RTX 4070 SUPER: gets r5 with its own bundle, rtx4070super-r5-srcg50-int8, at about 400 fps.
- RTX 3090: the only bundle it fits is the portable ampere-plus-r5-srcg50-int8. That bundle is not in S3 yet, and the restore step defaults to required. So after the push, every 3090 boot ends in VAST_ONSTART FAILED and no server starts. That is worse than today: origin/main (49e58d4) boots the old fast recipe and serves.
- Tesla T4: fits no bundle. It boots r5's serving levers with eager UNet and compiled TAESD. No .ts engine is built at HEAD, while origin/main would try to build one.

The local archive at tmp/trt_bundle/musetalk-trt-r5-ampere-plus.tar.gz matches the pinned sha256, so the upload is the only missing piece. Nothing has run on a 3090 yet. Both loaders require the cross-GPU probe check (relative L2 ≤ 0.01) to pass, and with no silent fallback a failure there fails the boot. 3090 fps is unknown.

Avatar creation (POST /avatars/prepare) is installed by SETUP_FULL_STACK=1 and works on Ampere GPUs. Prepared avatars upload to S3 and are restored after a restart.

Every container restart repeats a full first boot. The template deletes /workspace/MuseTalk and SETUP_CLEAN=1 rebuilds the venv each time, so each restart redoes:
- a 3.38 GB clone
- deleting and rebuilding the 9.5 GB venv
- about 5.7 GB of weights, including a Google Drive file
- the bundle download (1.0 GB on a 3090, 2.58 GB on a 4070 SUPER)

The runtime secret cannot change this, because the install runs before the secret is read. Repo-side changes could.

The template as pasted contains the bootstrap AWS access key pair in plain text. Rotate it. That changes only the two key values in the template.

Evidence paths are relative to /workspace/MuseTalk. The injected-facts bundle-check run and the extracted mmcv extension are in /tmp/claude-0/-workspace/866169db-0af2-4cde-9a98-79a398efeda7/scratchpad/vast_audit/trace/. I made no AWS calls, so S3 object presence and the secret's contents come from the commit message, the docs and the task context.

checks.item: Template: flock lock and ERR/EXIT traps
checks.detail: flock -n on fd 9 (/tmp/musetalk-onstart.lock) makes a concurrent second run exit 0 with one message and no VAST_ONSTART marker. fd 9 passes down to vast_onstart.sh and then to the server and coturn: vast_server_ctl.sh starts them with setsid nohup and never closes it. So the lock is held for the server's lifetime, and re-running the template by hand in a live container exits 0 at once. A container restart kills those processes and frees the lock. The ERR trap only echoes '[bootstrap] failed at line N'; set -e then exits non-zero. vast_onstart.sh prints exactly one VAST_ONSTART COMPLETE or FAILED marker. The EXIT trap removes STAGE_DIR, which is a no-op after the mv. A SIGKILL during the clone can leave /workspace/MuseTalk.stage.* behind, up to about 3.4 GB each.

Dimension: the serving venv here compared with a fresh `install_musetalk.sh --clean` run from the unchanged template, at HEAD e0d0985. SP below means /workspace/.venvs/musetalk_trt_stagewise/lib/python3.10/site-packages.

Kokoro is on by default, legacy-int8 is off, and the matrix is auto. Both an RTX 3090 and an RTX 4070 SUPER get cu121; I confirmed this with the helper's injected-host-facts hook.

**If the install finished**, it would rebuild this venv almost exactly: 210 of the 214 distributions here, all at identical versions. I computed this from this venv's METADATA; the same method reproduces the recorded 09-28 pip dry-run exactly (177/177). The 4 missing ones are the legacy-int8 group: nvidia-modelopt, nvidia-modelopt-core, PuLP and torchprofile. Neither serving nor avatar prep imports them. Only the engine-build tools import `modelopt`, lazily.

**BLOCKER: the install does not finish, on HEAD or on origin/main.**
- The first avatar-prep pip call is `pip install openmim setuptools<81 ninja psutil -c constraints-cu121.txt` (install_musetalk.sh:645).
- That pulls openmim 0.3.9 → opendatalab 0.0.10 → openxlab 0.1.3, which requires `rich~=13.4.2`.
- The constraints pin rich==15.0.0. typer 0.27.2 (from the Kokoro group) also needs rich>=13.8.0, so no single rich version satisfies both.
- pip therefore stops with ResolutionImpossible. The step is not optional, so the installer exits and vast_onstart.sh prints VAST_ONSTART FAILED before secrets, TURN, the bundle or the server. A fresh Vast box serves nothing at all, not just no avatar prep.
- This venv only has the combination because Kokoro was hand-installed with uv on 09-27. `pip check` here reports exactly this conflict. The dry-run that validated the constraints left out the avatar-prep group.
- Fix in the repo, no template change: stop installing openmim's dependency chain (`--no-deps openmim`, or drop it from install_musetalk.sh:645 and requirements/avatar-prep.in:88 together). Nothing imports mim, openxlab or opendatalab. The git-tracked mmcv wheel means the mim fallback never runs. Then prove it with one real clean full-stack install.

**Package versions for r5.** All pinned and identical to this venv: torch 2.5.1+cu121, torch_tensorrt 2.5.0 (PyPI build), TensorRT 10.3.0 (all three packages), onnx 1.17.0, diffusers 0.30.2, transformers 4.39.2, aiortc 1.14.0, av 16.1.0, numpy 1.23.5, opencv 4.9.0.80, triton 3.1.0, and the CUDA 12.1 wheels. Two things sit outside the constraints file:
- the mmcv wheel, which is identical to the one installed here and has sm_86-only kernels (fine on a 3090 and a 4070 SUPER);

verdicts.item: Control-plane registration keys (LINGUA_*) are not in the secret
verdicts.reason:
The code matches the auditor's description. A worker registers only when it has LINGUA_WORKER_TOKEN, plus LINGUA_CONTROL_PLANE_BASE_URL (or both explicit URLs), plus a public base_url it can discover. With none of these it logs 'integration disabled' and /health returns 200. The one direct look at the secret (the 2026-09-15 template boot) exported 10 names, none of them LINGUA_*. The current content is still unknown: the runtime key cannot even DescribeSecret. This box registers only because vast_server_ctl.sh sources /workspace/.lingua-control-plane.env. That file holds 8 key names: LINGUA_WORKER_TOKEN, LINGUA_CONTROL_PLANE_BASE_URL, LINGUA_WORKER_BASE_URL, VAST_INSTANCE_ID, WORKER_ID, LINGUA_WORKER_GPU_TYPE, LINGUA_WORKER_DEFAULT_CAPACITY and LINGUA_WORKER_CALLBACK_REQUIRED.

Corrections and additions:
(a) The '2026-09-28 bootstrap-written copy' is an inference from the file's header and mtime. Both 2026-09-28 onstart runs skipped the secret, so the file does not prove the secret's content that day, though it is consistent with it.
(b) The failure mode is worse than 'wait for registration'. A partial LINGUA config (for example a token and a register URL but no heartbeat URL), or a missing 8000/tcp mapping, sets control_plane_requested=true but configured=false. The status is then 'unhealthy' and /health returns 503 permanently: no registration loop even starts. Every boot then fails at 1800 s with no recovery, and new sessions also get 503 while the worker is registering.
(c) On a template boot, Vast's PID-1 environment has CONTAINER_ID, PUBLIC_IPADDR and VAST_TCP_PORT_8000 (all present on this Vast box). A fresh worker therefore gets its own worker_id and base_url without WORKER_ID or VAST_INSTANCE_ID, so the advice not to copy per-instance keys into the secret is right. LINGUA_WORKER_CALLBACK_REQUIRED is also safe for the whole fleet: with it set, start fails fast when the token or URL is missing.
(d) The documented architecture routes calls through the EC2 worker registry, so an unregistered worker most likely gets no platform calls. The backend is not in the repo, so this stays unknown.

Why the auditor's grep missed it: torch_tensorrt 2.5.0 queries the device while the module loads. The class body of TRTInterpreter has a default argument CompilationSettings(). Its field default_factory=default_device calls torch.cuda.current_device(), and with CUDA hidden that raises.

Why the install fails: on any GPU host, libcuda.so.1 loads, so the smoke counts this as 'failed', not 'deferred' (ok=False, exit 1). The smoke is a mandatory run_strict_step, so the installer exits and vast_onstart prints VAST_ONSTART FAILED.

Scope:
- It hits every fresh Vast boot, including server-only ones, on HEAD and on origin/main (the installer is identical).
- Today it is hidden behind the openmim blocker, and the uncommitted working-tree fix does not touch it.
- The planned CUDA-hidden smoke run (startup_import_smoke) was never recorded; only the unit tests and a find_spec-only --check ran.

Fix (repo only, no template change): in the CUDA-hidden smoke, treat gpu_stack import failures as deferred, or drop torch_tensorrt from it and import it in the GPU self-test instead.
